findings.reason: Standalone in-process hub diagnostic whose CLI has no outcome-count or performance rejection oracle: run returns tick mean/p99, maximum emitted packet bytes, finish count and sanction count, and main only prints them. Argument/setup failures still throw. The separate TestGhostLoadTest supplies the actual 32 normal finishes / 5 sanctions plus 11 healthy finishes assertions. Synthetic time advances 50 ms per tick without wall-clock sleeping; only room.tick is timed, excluding publishTick ingress work. Default 32 bots and five simulated seconds are bounded and ROM/graphics/socket-free, but up to 256 bots and one simulated hour are accepted. findings.reason: Standalone real-loopback integration/stress tool with an explicit CLI rejection oracle: unsuccessful reports throw. It checks room membership and unique sessions, overflow rejection, mixed-mode sanction/isolation/recovery, decoded remote poses, accepted finish timing/identity, complete unique standings pages, next-round reconnect, room removal and server shutdown. Report success additionally requires exact completed-cycle/lifecycle totals and positive ghost/ping observations. Default is four players, one traffic second and one cycle; opt-in limits reach transport capacity, 600 seconds and 100 cycles. Real countdowns, authentication, sockets/proxy and cleanup contribute cost beyond the traffic window. CPU/heap/GC cover the colocated server plus clients/proxy; no absolute timing threshold. Synthetic poses and NONE verification state do not validate engine replay.
findings.opportunity: Keep the existing bounded JUnit transport matrix and explicit larger CLI stress runs distinct. Retain per-player pose and complete-standings checks when tuning overhead. Reuse source-matched runs rather than duplicating the same matrix, and never interpret whole-process metrics as server-only capacity or a successful run as a latency budget pass.

findings.reason: Standalone ROM-free multi-process relay measurement with a correctness/lifecycle oracle, not a speed threshold. Parent requires successful child reports and exits, all expected room tick observations, zero remaining rooms, released listener and successful owned-process/file cleanup; main throws on an unsuccessful report. Load children check measured ghost/browser/admission/ping activity, per-frame synthetic pose equality and cross-room ownership, accepted timed standings and lifecycle recovery. Static cost: one server JVM plus one load/proxy JVM per 1/2/4 rooms, identity provisioning, real admission/countdown/warmup/measurement windows and JFR; each child uses a 1 GiB maximum heap. Default traffic window is ten seconds plus two seconds warmup, excluding setup/cleanup; no measured duration is claimed.
findings.opportunity: Retain process separation because it gives server-versus-generator attribution absent from socket-stress. Keep capacity cells explicit and isolated; the existing small two-room JUnit scenario is already bounded. Do not turn reported CPU, sampled memory or reservoir latency values into correctness thresholds, or merge server and generator costs without disclosing host contention. Preserve cross-room pose/standing and cleanup checks.

findings.reason: Standalone rendered demonstration with meaningful bounded integration assertions, not a benchmark or image oracle. It rejects loss of participants, premature title-screen return, player death, missing natural finish, renderer ghost cap above eight, missing standing/page counts and visible-player finish; at 16+ players it also requires a mid-pack rank and visibility churn. The peer helper counts standing slots/pages and finds the visible player by name; it does not independently validate every row against expected timing/identity as socket-stress does. Encoder failure/timeout and collected cleanup failures reject process success. Static cost includes optional separate ROM-rendered route preparation, one live rendered/audio client, up to 255 protocol bots, real-time pacing, per-frame logs and ffmpeg. Cosmetic bots retime recorded poses; this is not 256 gameplay simulations.

findings.reason: Standalone capture prerequisite with a narrow route-completion oracle. It replays the maintained GHZ1 controller movie from frame 840 through a fresh ROM-backed, surfaceless-EGL capture session, renders every step, rejects player death and absence of natural completion, then writes bounded cosmetic poses with first-input metadata. Route parsing enforces magic, size/count and metadata bounds. There is no comparison against native/reference poses or expected completion time; bots subsequently retime this output. Static cost is a full ROM route simulation plus per-frame rendering and retained poses, not just serializing a fixture.
findings.opportunity: Classify as a route/visual-data generator with completion checks, not an independent parity test. Retain real-input completion provenance. For repeated captures, use the capacity tool existing recorded-route argument with a source/ROM/movie-matched artifact; do not assume the file format embeds that provenance. Do not remove rendering merely as a cost fix without checking which presentation state determines the exported poses.

findings.reason: ROM-backed validation-profile generator, not a validation test. It derives dimensions and writes output but compares neither expected geometry nor complete catalog coverage. Missing ROMs print Skipping and continue; even zero profiles are written successfully, potentially to the default resource path. Runtime/load/overflow/I/O failures can throw, which is incidental rejection rather than an independent correctness oracle. Validation value is low as a gate, while asset-generation value remains useful. Intended complete execution loads every eligible act across available S1/S2/S3K ROMs, so static cost is high; a cheap all-missing run proves nothing. The separate TestBundledProfileSource checks bundled catalog coverage.
findings.opportunity: Keep outside the executable-test count. Generate to a temporary destination and verify expected catalog keys before replacing the bundled table. A later explicit completeness/required-ROM mode would prevent accidental partial output; preserve any deliberately requested partial-generation use. Treat missing ROMs as absent evidence, not a successful all-game validation. No source change is proposed as already implemented.

findings.reason: Operational authenticated loopback readiness probe, not a JUnit or gameplay test. Missing/invalid config or token, HTTP errors, timeout/interruption and any status other than 204 cause status 1 and a nonzero process exit. Intended cost is one local HTTP request with a two-second connect timeout and three-second request timeout plus JVM/config startup. Its server endpoint returns 204 after authorization/method checking; it does not exercise room creation, relay data, uploads, replay verification, or an actor work round-trip. High value is scoped to this inexpensive supervisor readiness contract.
findings.opportunity: Retain as a small operational check and list it separately from suite coverage. Do not substitute it for deployment-smoke or count a 204 as end-to-end racing health. Existing tests exercise successful and failed health checks; no broad performance rewrite is justified by this entrypoint review.

measurement_status: Classifications describe the pinned source. The four-file implementation and fresh focused measurements are documented separately in the companion audit.
